pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 9.3.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: APOLOGY LETTER

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why do we write apology letters?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify key elements of an apology letter for comprehension
2. write an apology letter seeking reconciliation for effective communication
3. appreciate the use of letters in fostering peaceful co-existence in daily living

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter

Teach
• Focus skill: identify key elements of an apology letter for comprehension.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Writing 9.3.1 Functional Writing: Apology Letter
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we write apology letters?
2. what went well and why ● what did not go well and why?
3. what can be done differently next time?
4. what have they learnt?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
